Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36791: test: fix waitTipChanged timeout on slow hosts and use monotonic clock in interface_ipc_mining

46ee95db49c9fa7f4b80a1e59816660f5ee0c4f4 test: use time.monotonic() for durations in interface_ipc_mining (ViniciusCestarii)
9b6dadb39c22bfb6d8b8040519316768919ff906 test: fix waitTipChanged timeout on slow hosts in interface_ipc_mining (ViniciusCestarii)

Pull request description:

  Follow up suggested in https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36731#issuecomment-6675432663.

  The first commit fix the timeout on a slow host and the second one use time.monotonic() for durations.

  Command to reproduce the errors with a simulated slow wall clock:
  ```
  faketime --exclude-monotonic -f "+0 x0.1" build/test/functional/interface_ipc_mining.py
  ```

Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36105: bitcoin wrapper: Fix Windows exec so wrapper waits for child process

ad98271f512d89fb37cc1debe3a9319165210a22 bitcoin: Use generic_category for errno from exec/spawn CRT functions (Ryan Ofsky)
7fc08852e4b8852ec8a48b82ff90da17fe7fc342 test: Enable tool_bitcoin.py and interface_gui.py tests on Windows (Ryan Ofsky)
4453ead3270b0a63a224fbcb67d15a4ea4ceb5d7 util: Fix ExecVp on Windows to wait for child process (Ryan Ofsky)

Pull request description:

  **Problem**: On Windows, `bitcoin.exe` spawns a child process and immediately exits rather than waiting for it to finish. This breaks capturing output and checking exit codes in scripts and tests.

  **Solution**: Switch `util::ExecVp` from `_execvp` to `_spawnvp(_P_WAIT)`, which blocks until the child exits and forwards its exit code. Also enable `tool_bitcoin.py` and `interface_gui.py` tests which were skipped due to previous behavior.

  This fix requires small changes to `src/util/exec.cpp` and `src/bitcoin.cpp` and there is also an extra commit fixing `errno` message strings on Windows when `ExecVp` fails. Details in commit messages.

commit.message:
Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36408: test: allow 3 bytes of fee overestimate in assert_fee_amount

050409b2c5522eff0dc37c00a6d1225a8a437e17 test: allow 3 bytes of fee overestimate in assert_fee_amount (Ferdinando Ametrano)

Pull request description:

  The wallet sizes a transaction assuming a 71-byte low-R ECDSA signature. A signature whose r or s has leading zero bytes is shorter, so the fee can cover a few bytes more than the signed transaction needs. In #36394 the wallet estimated 219 bytes and paid 438 sat at 2 sat/vB, but the signed transaction was 216 bytes: the signature was 3 bytes short. That happens about once in 4 million signatures. `assert_fee_amount` allows only 2 bytes of overestimate, so the test failed.

  I raise the allowance to 3 bytes, which makes the failure about 200 times rarer. The check that the fee is not too low is unchanged. maflcko suggested 3 bytes in #24151 and #25164.

  Fixes #36394.

  *Made with my usual tools: a computer, the Internet and an LLM. The mistakes, as usual, are all mine.*

commit.message:
Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36757: net: ignore privacy network peer's view of our address

9cfd6014005197d9d2d67dacb3c079980e3b284c test: check privacy-network peers' view of our address is not used (stratospher)
533fee6b9da3801612f245af461fb2d8fb06f197 net: ignore privacy-network peers' view of our address (stratospher)

Pull request description:

  privacy networks set `addrMe` ("IP address peer thinks I am") in the VERSION message [as all zeroes](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/f103de70de0662a1395dca2e536cf5872d86eaa2/src/net_processing.cpp#L1667).
  this PR ensures we ignore it when processing VERSION message.

  this fixes a fingerprint which makes it possible to correlate clearnet and privacy network IPs but it requires some not so easy preconditions:
  1. we need to choose this adversarial tor/i2p peer to make an outbound connection to from our addrman
  2. we need to be using a unique enough port. this would become easier in a future if we ever support random ports.

  h/t to Loupe and instagibbs for finding this fingerprint!

Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36068: fuzz: reuse one fuzzed wallet across inputs

2553b4cd9678f9d7ba78be3573eb3cd095ab3ea6 wallet: add test-only helper to clear in-memory transaction state (brunoerg)

Pull request description:

  FuzzedWallet was rebuilt for every input. That imports eight
  descriptors, and each address it then hands out costs a BIP32
  derivation plus three separate WalletBatch transactions (see
  DescriptorScriptPubKeyMan::GetNewDestination) - all paid before the
  target reaches the code under test.

  This PR changes it to build the wallet once in the target's .init hook and
  reset it perinput instead. I benchmarked on my Ubuntu machine without
  sanitizers and got a ~6x speedup.

commit.message:
fuzz: reuse one fuzzed wallet across inputs

FuzzedWallet was rebuilt for every input. That imports eight
descriptors, and each address it then hands out costs a BIP32
derivation plus three separate WalletBatch transactions (see
DescriptorScriptPubKeyMan::GetNewDestination) - all paid before the
target reaches the code under test.

Build the wallet once in the target's .init hook and reset it per
input instead.

wallet: add test-only helper to clear in-memory transaction state

Add CWallet::ClearInMemoryTxStateForTest(), which drops mapWallet,
wtxOrdered, mapTxSpends, m_txos and m_locked_coins, leaving the
database, the wallet flags and the ScriptPubKeyMans untouched.

This exists so that fuzz harnesses can reuse a single wallet across
inputs instead of rebuilding it for every one. m_txos and mapTxSpends
are private, so a harness cannot reset them on its own.

RemoveTxs() is not usable here: it erases each transaction's
m_it_wtxOrdered from wtxOrdered, and that iterator is only valid for
transactions added through AddToWallet(). Harnesses that populate
mapWallet directly leave it uninitialized.

Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36824: ci: Switch to self-hosted CDash

f16d5166a26a1e8b9539297dc960d7cde28778bf ci: Switch to self-hosted CDash (will)

Pull request description:

  Switch our CDash submissions from my.cdash.org to our self-hosted instance at https://cdash.fish.foo/index.php?project=bitcoin-core.

  my.cdash.org sometimes deletes our logs extremely quickly. That leaves too little time to investigate failures and makes links to earlier results 404, which is annoying.

  The new instance runs on a dedicated Hetzner VPS and gives us control over retention. Submissions are configured to be retained for 90 days, and the project's build retention is also set to 90 days.

commit.message:
Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36556: depends: fix non-atomic reads in capnp debug assertions

6e8e85ddcf2eb4a062fab3cd2b9c046edfbf72ec depends: fix non-atomic reads in capnp debug assertions (xyzconstant)

Pull request description:

  KJ's debug assertions read the mutex futex word and `AtomicRefcounted` refcounts non-atomically. The TSan job builds capnp without optimization, which automatically enables these assertions, and TSan reports these reads as data races the moment KJ objects start communicating across threads.

  libmultiprocess enables cross-thread communication for the first time in bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess#376, which replaces the pipe used in `EventLoop::sync()` with `kj::Executor::executeSync()`. This is what triggered the [failure](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/actions/runs/38094008438/job/114336046070?pr=376).

  Patches are the upstream commits capnproto/capnproto@b91a6ba7c7 and capnproto/capnproto@cc13c8c45f, which are backports of the v2 fixes in capnproto/capnproto#2781 and capnproto/capnproto#2843 (backport PR: capnproto/capnproto#2855).
